verdict.rationale: Turso documents exporting a database as a plain SQL dump (`turso db shell your-database .dump > dump.sql`), an open, portable format. Its SQLite-compatible engine (libSQL is MIT open source) supports leaving. A community report notes that schemas using Turso-specific extensions stop working with standard SQLite tools, which limits how cleanly the data can be taken elsewhere. Missing for 10: bulk export across all databases in an account, documented portability of extension-specific features (e.g. vectors) to other systems, an account exit/deletion process, and independent hands-on corroboration of a full migration out.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: You can always dump your production database and use it locally for development
They are fully SQLite-compatible — they open existing SQLite files
libSQL is an open source, open contribution fork of SQLite, created and maintained by Turso.
